clue.text: The females are better!

parts.note: reads as a boast that women outdo men, but completes the stock phrase for wives, the 'better' partners in a marriage

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that women are superior to men.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the missing word to 'better' and you get the jocular phrase for wives: each is her husband's better half, and together they are the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Wives are called 'better halves', so the females are the better portions of each couple.

clue.text: Underground club that needed an army of stokers?

definitions.text: Underground club that needed an army of stokers?

parts.words: Underground club that needed an army of stokers?
parts.note: a secret society read as one located in the inferno below, whose flames need constant feeding

explanation.surface: A secret society that kept a crew of furnace men busy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hellfire Club was an 18th-century society of rakes; 'underground' suggests both secrecy and the place below, whose flames need stoking.
explanation.definitionFit: The eternal flames of damnation would need stokers, and the 18th-century rakes' society took that name.

clue.text: One ruffled but in line has a kingly' air

indicators.note: 'in line' places the shuffled word inside the word line

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ruffled hair is disordered, so the letters of one are disarranged

explanation.surface: A dishevelled person who stands in a queue with regal bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffled' signals the anagram and 'in' the container; 'but' and 'has a' are link words, and 'air' just finishes the surface's picture of regal bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is the king of beasts, so lion-like bearing is regal.

clue.text: Sometimes an expensive break …fast in Tsarist Russia ?

definitions.text: Sometimes an expensive break …fast in Tsarist Russia

parts.words: Sometimes an expensive break …fast in Tsarist Russia
parts.note: breakfast split into 'break fast': the Tsars' jewelled Fabergé gifts were for the end of Lent, a fast

explanation.surface: Suggests that breakfast in imperial Russia was a costly meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'breakfast' as 'break fast': the end of Lent's fast is marked by a gift, and Fabergé's jewelled ones for the Tsars were very costly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tsars gave jeweled Fabergé ovoids at the festival ending Lent's fast.

clue.text: Snake with one band towering up

parts.note: the asp is a small venomous snake
the Roman numeral for one is I
a ring is a band, as of metal round a finger

explanation.surface: A snake with a stripe rearing itself upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aspiring rises or soars upward, as a spire reaching skyward.

clue.text: In unusual need, turn pets in to this officer

indicators.note: an unusual version of the words is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: Told to hand pets over to a police chief in unusual need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of NEED plus TURN PETS IN, fourteen in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior police rank above inspector, or the official in charge of a department.

clue.text: I would almost get up to the giant

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is cut

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone nearly managing to climb up to meet a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RISE to RIS. Idris is the giant of Welsh legend who gives Cader Idris, a Welsh mountain, its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh legend names a giant astronomer whose seat was the mountain Cader Idris.

clue.text: Fill one ruined temple

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: a ruined building is broken apart, so the letters of temple are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone filling in a single ruined temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges TEMPLE as MPLETE. The answer is an archaic verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb from Latin 'implere', to fill up, as in 'replete'.

clue.text: Examination of Alfred and Frederick ?

parts.note: two kings each known by the same epithet, which is also an Oxford honours exam

explanation.surface: Asks about a test taken by two men named Alfred and Frederick.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred of Wessex and Frederick of Prussia both carry the title 'the Great'; the plural is the name of the Oxford final classics exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's final honours exam in classics is so called, and two kings carry the matching title.

clue.text: One of the good folk of Utah

definitions.text: One of the good folk of Utah

parts.words: One of the good folk of Utah
parts.note: the good folk are holy people, and Utah is the home of the Mormon church

explanation.surface: Describes one of the virtuous residents of a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Mormons call themselves by the name of their church, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, based in Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mormon is a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, centred in Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Be quick to make appearances with a music-maker

parts.note: looks are someone's appearance, how they seem
a harp is an instrument, something that makes music

explanation.surface: An instruction to hurry along and turn up with a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Look sharp!' is an idiom urging someone to hurry up.

clue.text: Anna made a contribution to it

definitions.text: Anna made a contribution to it

parts.words: Anna made a contribution to it
parts.note: Anna looks like a woman's name, but an anna was a small Indian coin, one sixteenth of the larger unit of currency

explanation.surface: A woman named Anna chipped in to some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The anna was an Indian coin worth a sixteenth of the main unit, so sixteen annas 'contributed' to make one.
explanation.definitionFit: India's currency unit was divided into sixteen annas, each a fraction of the whole coin.

clue.text: "The leader is But all are divine" (Arnold)

definitions.text: "The leader is But all are divine" (Arnold)

parts.words: "The leader is But all are divine" (Arnold)
parts.note: a line of Matthew Arnold's verse with one word missing, a superlative of beauty describing the leader of a divine group

explanation.surface: A quotation from the poet Matthew Arnold with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash where the missing word goes; the verse praises a leader as the most beautiful of a band of divine beings.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of 'fair' means most beautiful, the quality the poem gives the leader above the rest.

clue.text: Relation creeps craftily to the Head

indicators.note: done craftily, the letters of creeps are worked into a new order by cunning
the head of the word 'the' is its first letter, its top

explanation.surface: A relative sneaks slyly up to the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' reworks CREEPS into RESPEC; 'Head' takes the first letter of 'the', T. 'Relation' here is the sense in the phrase 'with respect to'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In respect of' means 'in relation to', so the two nouns share the sense of reference or bearing.

clue.text: Make fast the bird

definitions.meaning: to secure a rope by threading it through a block or ring, a sailor's term
the female of the ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: An order to tie up a bird securely.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors reeve a line through a ring to secure it; the female ruff, a sandpiper, carries the same name.

clue.text: Distinguished like John Gilpin ?

parts.note: William Cowper's comic poem opens by calling its hero a citizen 'of credit and renown'

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is as famous as the hero of a comic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gilpin is the London linen-draper of William Cowper's ballad, introduced as 'a citizen of credit and renown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famous and widely honoured is to be distinguished, as Cowper's draper was said to be.

clue.text: A pigeon for Lennox Robinson's boy.?

definitions.text: A pigeon for Lennox Robinson's boy

parts.words: A pigeon for Lennox Robinson's boy
parts.note: a pigeon with a pale crown, and the Irish playwright's comedy about a favoured son

explanation.surface: Suggests giving a dove to a playwright's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Lennox Robinson wrote the Irish comedy 'The Whiteheaded Boy'; a pale-crowned pigeon is described the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson's comedy is about a pampered son with a pale crown, and a pigeon so coloured is named for its pale crown.

clue.text: Connected with an iron

parts.note: reads like something linked with a flatiron or golf club, but means joined by molten alloy from a hot tool

explanation.surface: Something linked to a domestic iron or a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: An iron here is the heated tool that melts a fusible alloy to join wires or metal parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal parts joined with melted alloy from a hot tool are fused this way.

clue.text: Untidy large bed in Coventry

indicators.note: an untidy arrangement scatters the letters of large bed into a messy new order

explanation.surface: A messy king-size bed in a Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' scrambles LARGE BED. 'in Coventry' points to the Belgrade Theatre in Coventry, an English Midlands city; the phrase also means being ostracised, a false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry's civic playhouse bears the Serbian capital's name, which gave timber for its building.

clue.text: Implying, that Forficula is serious in home-seeking?

definitions.text: Implying, that Forficula is serious in home-seeking?

parts.words: Implying, that Forficula is serious in home-seeking?
parts.note: Forficula is the earwig genus, said in folklore to seek a home in a person's ear

explanation.surface: Wonders whether an insect is in earnest about finding a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Forficula is the earwig's Latin genus; split the answer to read 'ear nest', the home the earwig is said to seek.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sincere and grave in intent is the plain sense; the split reading gives a nest in an ear.

clue.text: Let's'& shorten' the preliminaries

parts.note: suggests cutting the opening formalities, and the clipped form of the word for an opening is the result

explanation.surface: A suggestion to cut the formalities short.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks for the shortened form of the word meaning an opening or preliminary.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped form of 'introduction' names the opening part of a piece or a presentation.

clue.text: One of Carlyle's gigmanity in the wilds ?

definitions.text: One of Carlyle's gigmanity in the wilds

parts.words: One of Carlyle's gigmanity in the wilds
parts.note: Carlyle mocked the respectable as those who keep a gig; a trap is another light carriage, so its keeper is one of them

explanation.surface: Asks about a respectable gentleman out in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Carlyle coined 'gigmanity' for respectable folk who kept a gig; a trap is another small carriage, and a man who catches animals for fur in the wilds has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter who snares animals for their fur in the backwoods; the word also suggests a man owning a trap.

clue.text: Drives out the civets

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of civets are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Somebody chases the civet cats away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CIVETS; it also completes the sense 'drives out', which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to drive a tenant from a property by legal process.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical exponents of brinkmanship?

parts.note: a verge is a brink, so those who go to the verge are church officers who carry a staff

explanation.surface: Wonders which churchmen enjoy taking risks at the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Brinkmanship is going to the brink; a verge is also a brink or edge, so church officers named after their verge (a staff of office) play on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Church officers who carry a rod before dignitaries take their title from the verge, and a verge is an edge.

clue.text: In Whitechapel I and another have a lamb-like air

annotationWithheld.why: In Whitechapel I and another have a lamb-like air: ELIAN means in the style of Elia (Charles Lamb), but no reading of 'In Whitechapel I and another' yields the letters ELIAN with each word doing one job
annotationWithheld.clue: In Whitechapel I and another have a lamb-like air

clue.text: Conservative to the last ?

parts.note: a stubborn traditionalist who holds out until death, from the phrase for something slow to perish

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone will stay a Tory until they die.
explanation.walkthrough: A stubborn reactionary resists to the end, as if refusing to give up life easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn traditionalist resists change until death, the image in the idiom for dying slowly.

clue.text: Very dear, a French novel

definitions.meaning: the French for darling or beloved
a 1920 novel by Colette about a young lover

explanation.surface: A costly French book.
explanation.definitionFit: French 'darling', and the title of Colette's novel about a young man kept by an older courtesan.

clue.text: Ivy was his show-girl.

parts.note: Ivy looks like a dancer's name, but a bush of ivy was hung outside a tavern as its sign

explanation.surface: A man whose girlfriend Ivy worked in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Old taverns hung an ivy bush outside as their sign (hence 'good wine needs no bush'), so ivy was what the landlord showed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern landlord displayed ivy as his trade sign, so the plant served as the publican's advertisement.

clue.text: Quality of Old Nick that shows, gratitude-in healthy-mindedness

indicators.note: the word for thanks is set in the middle of the word for soundness of mind

parts.note: sanity is soundness of mind
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A devil's trait revealed as thankfulness within a sound mind.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for 'thank you'. Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is the Devil, and this word names his diabolical nature.

clue.text: Loved a party with one Biddy

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
red biddy is cheap red wine laced with meths, so red is one kind of biddy

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a party with a woman called Biddy.
explanation.walkthrough: Biddy looks like an Irish woman's name; red biddy is old British slang for cheap red wine mixed with methylated spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adored is to be worshipped or deeply cherished.
